title: Work–energy theorem
examples: How do I find the work done if the force changes with distance?
Is the work done related to the change in speed?
What is the difference between constant and variable force work?

explain.say: The work-energy theorem connects work done to energy change.

items: Work done (W) equals the change in kinetic energy (ΔKE).
This means W equals the final KE minus the initial KE.

draw.text: Work done = Change in Kinetic Energy

explain.say: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion for an object.

draw.text: KE = one half m v squared

explain.say: For a constant force, work is simply force times distance.

items: W = F d | Force times distance

explain.say: When force changes, work is the area under the force graph.
Consider a force graph from zero to three meters.
In real life, a spring pulls a cart slowly.

faq.q: Does the work-energy theorem only work for straight lines?
faq.a: No, it applies even when the force is changing direction or magnitude. You must still calculate the net work done.
asks: Does the path matter for work?
Can I use this if the force isn't straight?

faq.q: If the object stops, what is the work done?
faq.a: If the object stops, its final kinetic energy is zero. Therefore, the net work done must equal the negative of its initial kinetic energy.
asks: If vfinal is zero, what is W?
What is the work if it comes to rest?

faq.q: How do I calculate the area under a curved force graph?
faq.a: You must use calculus, specifically integration, to find the exact area under the curve between the start and end points.
asks: What math do I use for curved graphs?
Is there a simple formula for curved work?

faq.q: Is the work done by friction included in the calculation?
faq.a: Yes, friction is a force, so the work done by friction must be included. It usually removes energy from the system.
asks: How does friction affect the energy?

faq.q: What is the difference between work and potential energy?
faq.a: Work is the energy transferred by a force over a distance. Potential energy is stored energy due to position or state.
asks: Are work and energy the same thing?
Where does potential energy come from?

facts: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.
Kinetic energy is calculated using the formula one half times mass times velocity squared.
For a variable force, the work done is found by calculating the area under the force versus distance graph.
The units for both work and energy are Joules.

quiz.say: A box starts from rest and accelerates to a speed of ten meters per second. If its mass is five kilograms, what is the net work done?
quiz.why: The initial KE is zero, so W equals the final KE: one half times five times ten squared, which is two hundred fifty Joules.

wrong.0: This incorrectly calculates mass times velocity squared, forgetting the one half factor.
wrong.1: This incorrectly calculates mass times velocity, ignoring the squared term.
wrong.3: This incorrectly uses only the mass times velocity, forgetting the one half factor.

quiz.say: If the force acting on an object varies linearly from zero to twenty newtons over a distance of five meters, what is the work done?
quiz.why: The graph forms a triangle, so the area is one half times the base times the height: one half times five times twenty, which is one hundred Joules.

wrong.1: This incorrectly states the units as Newtons instead of Joules, forgetting the distance dimension.
wrong.2: This incorrectly calculates the area as a rectangle (20 times 5), ignoring the triangular shape.
wrong.3: This incorrectly calculates the work using only the final force value.

quiz.say: A force graph is given. If the area under the curve from x equals zero to x equals four is calculated, what physical quantity does this area represent?
quiz.why: The area under a force versus distance graph always calculates the total work done on the object.

wrong.1: Force is represented by the height on the graph, not the area.
wrong.2: While work equals KE, the area calculation itself represents the general work done, which is the primary concept here.
wrong.3: Acceleration is related to force, but the area represents energy transfer, not acceleration.
